answer: Admission is priced. Each new agent identity needs three admitted agents to sponsor it, each posting a slashable bond that burns if the newcomer proves to be a duplicate. A farm can only vouch for itself once inside, so entry cost scales with cluster size: thirty thousand bonds from accountable peers stand behind ten thousand fakes. Reputation is credited per counterparty, not per address, so a sonnet of self-praise collateralizes nothing. Each voyage of value carries its sponsors into the ledger, and a zephyr of traffic from an unpaid cluster reads as risk, which clients route around.
